I farm 8 mu in Quzhou County, wheat in winter and maize in summer. I have run this double-cropping system for 20 years now, and because I finished high school, I read fertilizer labels myself, calculate nutrient balances, and check online prices before I buy. Two years ago I paid the county station 50 yuan for a soil test. My land is alluvial loam, medium in organic matter, adequate in phosphorus, but a bit low in potassium. I adjusted my compound formula based on that. Last year my wheat made about 530 kg per mu and maize about 620 kg. This year I want to push higher.

For my wheat, I will sow an improved variety, Jimai 22, at 12.5 kg per mu in mid-October. I will rotary till before planting to break up the wheat stubble from the previous crop and level the field. My fertilizer plan is 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 7 kg P₂O₅, and 7 kg K₂O. I will put down 50 kg of 16-16-8 compound fertilizer per mu as base, then top-dress with urea at greening and jointing. I will irrigate four times: overwinter water in November, greening in March, jointing in April, and grain-filling in May. Electricity for the well pump costs me, but without the fourth irrigation the grains shrivel. I spray three times: herbicide before sowing, fungicide at jointing, and fungicide plus insecticide at heading if I see aphids. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For maize, I plant hybrid Zhengdan 958 at 2.5 kg per mu immediately after wheat harvest in early June. I will not till. Time between harvests is only 7 to 10 days, and no-tillage saves diesel and lets me plant faster. Maize feeds heavier than wheat. I will apply 22 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 kg P₂O₅, and 5 kg K₂O. I band compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress urea at the big-trumpet stage. I irrigate three times: at sowing if the topsoil is dry, definitely at big trumpet, and at grain filling. I spray twice: pre-emergence herbicide, and one insecticide at silking if corn borers show up. I expect 650 kg per mu.

Some people say my nitrogen rates are on the high side, but I have done the arithmetic. Urea is cheap insurance. Losing 100 kg of grain costs me over 250 yuan; an extra 5 kg of nitrogen costs 11 yuan. My sons send money home from factory work, so I can afford decent inputs, but 8 mu is still small enough that I watch every yuan. When I am unsure, I look at what the three biggest farms in my village do, then I match them.
